text.p: Following are the top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- In effort to stop them from falling prey to gangs, from October 1 under-16s will not be let into afternoon tea dances, and discotheques and restaurants selling alcohol and which have dance floors will also be out of bounds.
- Cambodia's royalist Funcinpec Party names new premier to succeed deposed First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh as parliament prepares to meet for the first time in seven months.
- A nationwide police manhunt underway for suspected serial killer wanted for murder of leading fashion designer Gianni Versace.
- Singapore's two boutiques selling clothes of designer Versace will be closed for one day to mark his death.
- Holidays in United States or Britain has become more expensive for Singaporeans because of strong US dollar and British sterling.
- Singaporeans make 1.1 million trips overseas in first four months of this year, 13 percent increase over same period last year.
- Trade in plunging kyat grinds to halt when Burma government detains traders over currency's nosedive against dollar-denominated foreign exchange certificates, witnesses say.
- Former Merrill Lynch banker at centre of multimillion-dollar fraud inquiry charged with money-laundering.
- Investors in Singapore and Indonesia react differently to QAF Ltd's proposed acquisition of majority stake in PT Indofood for some S$2.75 billion.
- Selling of Malaysian ringgit and Indonesian rupiah gathers steam, pushing two currencies to new lows against greenback.

- US stocks surge, pushing Dow Jones Industrial Average through 8,000, propelled by surprisingly strong profits from General Motors Corp and Intel Corp and smaller-than-expected rise in consumer prices.
- Cycle and Carriage shares sink to lowest level in almost a year, following analysts' downgrading of prospects for 1997.
- Mainboard-listed Lion Teck Chiang launches first phase of 202.3 hectare freehold industrial park project near Multimedia Super Corridor and new KL International Airport in Selangor.
- Keppel Bank launching fourth unit trust, this time aimed at newly listed shares in global market with emphasis on markets in Asia-Pacific region.
- Recently-listed books and stationery distributor Popular Holdings chalks up net earnings of S$7.9 million on turnover of S$161.7 million for the full year to April 30.
